messages:
Maria: quick question — we're seeing a customer hit duplicate side effects when the gateway retries streaming requests that the edge transforms (header rewrite + small body patch). upstream expects idempotency, but transforms change the canonical bytes so dedupe fails. do we lean on idempotency tokens or make the gateway responsible for abort-safety / single-commit semantics?
Arun: if the gateway mutates payloads then upstream can't assume identical bytes. options: 1) preserve an unmodified content-hash header the upstream can use to dedupe, 2) move non-idempotent transforms downstream (after dedupe), 3) make gateway detect+dedupe at proxy level. each has tradeoffs.
Kelsey: option 1 looks least invasive: add `X-Original-Checksum` + `X-Edge-Sig` so upstream can verify origin. downside: new header surface + signing keys. also need to think replay/TTL.
Tomas: for streaming aborts hedging is tricky — if client cancels but we already hedged to 2 upstreams, both could commit. maybe we need a gateway-level apply-once gate for routes that perform side effects. i.e., allow hedging for read-only routes only.
Clara: i'm wary of expanding headers. i'd prefer gateway-local dedupe: maintain a tiny store keyed by `Idempotency-Key` (or generated fingerprint) and gate forward unless we know we've seen it. That handles transformed bodies because dedupe key is independent.
Maria: sketch of a hybrid: 1) if `Idempotency-Key` present -> gateway ensures single-forward (use dedupe table). 2) else if client opts-in (`X-Allow-Gateway-Dedupe: true`) -> gateway uses ephemeral dedupe. 3) otherwise fallback to best-effort hedging but mark tracing/metrics so product teams can see risk.
Kelsey: we also need a secure ways to prove to upstream that a request was deduped at edge in case they need audit. maybe emit `X-Edge-Dedupe-Proof: sig` and an audit event to tracing.
Arun: storage/TTL for the dedupe table is the big cost. suggestion: store 128-bit fingerprint + route id + outcome code. TTL = max(hedge-window)+2m. estimate: at 10k req/s and 1 min TTL -> ~75M entries peak. that's non-trivial. need capacity planning.
Tomas: alternative: sharded LRU in-memory cache plus write-through to a compact persistent store (RocksDB) for longer TTLs. fast path is in-memory; misses consult local disk. risk: cross-pod duplicates if we don't coordinate.
Clara: can we get away with best-effort eventually-consistent cross-pod dedupe? many customers already accept low prob of duplication; we only need strong guarantees for a small set of routes (billing, order create). make those opt-in via route config.
Maria: agreed — plan: make strict single-commit behavior opt-in per route. default remains hedging-friendly read paths. action items: Kelsey prototype header-signed proof + tracing events; Tomas to sketch memory/disk hybrid and give rough cost; Arun to confirm protocol for `X-Original-Checksum` with upstream integrators. i'll draft an RFC outlining three modes (none/read-only,dedupe-at-edge,opt-in-strict) and tradeoffs.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> 2026-03-25T02:00:00Z (experiment: transform-dedupe-proto).
Kelsey: SGTM, i'll mock the header format: ``
X-Original-Checksum: sha256:abc123
X-Edge-Proof: v1.sig=base64
``
Arun: also include `x-edge-route-id` and `x-edge-instance` for audit.
Tomas: i'll send a rough cost calc by EOD tomorrow.
Clara: i'll update routing config to allow opt-in flag per route and add e2e testcases for cancel/hedge.
Maria: thanks all — i'll start RFC draft. ping me if you want to be co-authors. :thumbsup:
